interest: Shows a 1941 congressman's plea for lily-bulb imports from Japan, just before the asset freeze halted trade.
overview: Rep. Byrne asks State in 1941 whether harvested Japanese lily bulbs, already packed for shipment, can still enter the US to avert an Easter florist shortage; he later acknowledges State's reply.

people.name: Fletcher Warren
people.role: Executive Assistant to Assistant Secretary, Department of State

people.name: Sam Rayburn
people.role: Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives

people.name: Robert L. Doughton
people.role: Chairman, House Committee on Ways and Means

subfiles.about: Representative William T. Byrne requests State Department advice on whether harvested Japanese lily bulbs can be admitted into the United States.
subfiles.summary: Byrne relays florist Gloeckner's plea to admit already-packed Japanese lily bulbs before an Easter shortage.
subfiles.title: Letter from Representative William T. Byrne to Fletcher Warren on Japanese lily bulb imports

subfiles.about: An illegible enclosure, likely correspondence from Albany florist William C. Gloeckner concerning lily bulbs.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure page, likely Gloeckner's original letter on lily bulbs, is unreadable due to document degradation.
subfiles.title: Degraded enclosure regarding Japanese lily bulbs

subfiles.about: Representative William T. Byrne thanks Fletcher Warren for his August 30 letter regarding Japanese lily bulb imports.
subfiles.summary: Byrne thanks State for its reply on Japanese lily-bulb imports, closing the correspondence.
subfiles.title: Letter from Representative William T. Byrne to Fletcher Warren acknowledging correspondence
